gap: No result ChatGPT got states that DJI's own spec sheet caps the 100-120 V Power 1000 V2 at 20 A (2,400 W at 120 V, not the 2,600 W headline, which matches the 220-240 V model's 10.9 A), or that the same "2,600 W" on the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic is an X-Boost figure on an 1,800 W inverter.
standout_why: Compared against popsci.com (cited), willitrunpower.com and outagepowerguide.com. PopSci gives headline watts only: no surge, no boost mode, and no end-of-life percentage on any cycle figure. Willitrunpower already normalises cycle life (80% for EcoFlow/Anker/BLUETTI, 70% for Jackery) and marks X-Boost and Power Lifting as resistive-only, but for other models (Anker C1000 gen 1, RIVER 3 Plus, RIVER 2 Pro, AC180); it has no DJI, DELTA 3 Classic, C1000 Gen 2 or Elite 100 mini. Outagepowerguide has no cycle, boost or UPS figures. So the convention is partly covered, but nobody applies it to the models ChatGPT recommended.
decides: It confirms the order on continuous output but narrows it. On makers' figures at 120 V the order is DJI 2,400 W (my arithmetic from DJI's 20 A limit), Anker 2,000 W, EcoFlow 1,800 W, BLUETTI Elite 100 mini 700 W. ChatGPT's "2,600 W" for DJI is not supported by the 120 V spec row, and EcoFlow's 2,600 W is boost, not rated. On cycle life, only Anker and DJI publish a figure to 80% (4,000 cycles each); EcoFlow's US pages give no cycle count and BLUETTI's 6,000+ for the Elite 100 mini carries no percentage. Outside my angle but decisive: Anker's US store says all C1000 Gen 2 orders ship in 4–9 weeks, so it cannot be the pick from that store under the four-week rule. I could not read a US-seller price or page for the DJI. Of ours, the Elite 100 mini holds the light-load segment (700 W, 23.6 lb, $379 at BLUETTI). The ALLPOWERS P1800 is the 1,800 W row under $400 with code, but its 3,000+ cycles are to 70% in Dealectric's record, which I could not re-read.

findings.label: AC output limit, 100-120 V model (DYM1000V2L)
findings.value: AC 100-120 V, max current 20 A = 2,400 W at 120 V
findings.note: DJI gives amps, not watts, per regional model; 120 V × 20 A = 2,400 W is my arithmetic. The 220-240 V model (DYM1000V2H) is 10.9 A, and 240 V × 10.9 A = 2,616 W, which matches the 2,600 W headline. The page says "AC output data varies by country and region." 4 AC outlets on US/JP/CN versions.

findings.label: AC output in bypass mode (plugged into the wall), 100-120 V model
findings.value: max current 12 A = 1,440 W at 120 V
findings.note: 120 V × 12 A is my arithmetic. This is the limit while the unit passes wall power through.

findings.label: Cycle life and test conditions
findings.value: over 80% capacity after 4,000 cycles; LFP; 1,024 Wh
findings.note: DJI footnote: one cycle is a complete charge and discharge, tested at 25°C, recharged in Standard Mode, discharged at 1,000 W.

findings.label: Weight
findings.note: The lb figure is my conversion (14.2 × 2.2046). It is the heaviest of the 1 kWh candidates on makers' figures (Anker 24.9 lb, BLUETTI Elite 100 mini 23.6 lb, EcoFlow about 26.7 lb).
